method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the COPD-X Plan sections, not the citation. Recommendation grades (LoE/SoR) reproduced as the source states them.
source_coverage: C, O and X section pages retrieved in full. P and D sections NOT retrieved and listed unresolved.

claims.claim: COPD-X is the AU/NZ guideline by Lung Foundation Australia, endorsed by TSANZ; recommendations carry NHMRC LoE and GRADE SoR
claims.source_text: LoE = Level of evidence according National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) Evidence Hierarchy ... SoR = Strength of recommendation according to the GRADE ... developed and revised by Lung Foundation Australia ... endorsed by the Thoracic Society of Australia New Zealand (TSANZ)

claims.claim: Diagnosis rests on exertional breathlessness/cough/sputum, smoking or noxious exposure, and FEV1/FVC<0.7 post-bronchodilator
claims.source_text: Symptoms of exertional breathlessness, cough and sputum; A history of smoking, or exposure to other noxious agents; FEV1/FVC<0.7 post-bronchodilator

claims.claim: Confirm COPD with spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.7) — III-2, Strong
claims.source_text: | Confirm COPD with spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.7) | III-2 | Strong |

claims.claim: Smoking most important risk factor (I, Strong); smoking cessation reduces mortality (I, Strong)
claims.source_text: | Smoking is the most important risk factor for developing COPD | I | Strong | ... | Smoking cessation reduces mortality in people with COPD | I | Strong |

claims.claim: Large post-BD FEV1 increase, greater confidence if >15% and >400mL, might suggest asthma or coexisting asthma and COPD — III-2, Strong
claims.source_text: While a large increase in post-bronchodilator FEV₁ (with greater confidence if increase is >15% and >400mL) might suggest asthma or coexisting asthma and COPD ... | III-2 | Strong |

claims.claim: Chronic bronchitis is daily sputum production for at least three months of two or more consecutive years
claims.source_text: Chronic bronchitis is daily sputum production for at least three months of two or more consecutive years

claims.claim: Coexisting asthma in COPD 27% population-based, 28% hospital-based, from 19 studies; more frequent exacerbations with both
claims.source_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies found that the prevalence of coexisting asthma in patients with COPD was 27% in population-based studies and 28% in hospital-based studies ... found an increased frequency of exacerbations in patients with features of both asthma and COPD compared to those with COPD alone

claims.claim: Principal goals: stop smoking, optimise function via medications and pulmonary rehabilitation, prevent or treat aggravating factors and complications
claims.source_text: THE PRINCIPAL GOALS OF THERAPY are to stop smoking, to optimise function through symptom relief with medications and pulmonary rehabilitation, and to prevent or treat aggravating factors and complications

claims.claim: Regularly check inhaler technique and adherence — I, Strong
claims.source_text: | Regularly check inhaler technique and adherence | I | Strong |

claims.claim: Pulmonary rehabilitation and regular exercise recommended to anyone with COPD — I, Strong
claims.source_text: | Recommend non-pharmacological strategies such as pulmonary rehabilitation and regular exercise to anyone with COPD | I | Strong |

claims.claim: Lung volume reduction is I but WEAK; early palliative care is II and WEAK
claims.source_text: | Lung volume reduction (surgical and endobronchial) ... | I | Weak | | Consider palliative care early ... | II | Weak |

claims.claim: Adherence to inhaled regimens associated with reduced death and exacerbation admissions, RR 0.56 (95% CI 0.48-0.65)
claims.source_text: Adherence to inhaled medication regimes is associated with reduced risk of death and admissions to hospital due to exacerbations in COPD... 44% improvement (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.65)

claims.claim: Exacerbation diagnosed on changes in baseline dyspnoea, cough and/or sputum exceeding normal day-to-day variation, acute in onset
claims.source_text: Diagnose a COPD exacerbation based on changes in the patient's baseline dyspnoea, cough, and/or sputum that exceed normal day-to-day variations, are acute in onset, and may warrant a change in regular medication or hospital admission | III-2 | Strong

claims.claim: Inhaled short-acting bronchodilators first-line for exacerbations — I, Strong
claims.source_text: | Initiate inhaled short-acting bronchodilators as a first-line treatment of exacerbations | I | Strong |

claims.claim: Systemic corticosteroids oral where possible, 30 to 50mg daily for 5 days — I, Strong
claims.source_text: Consider prescribing systemic corticosteroids to reduce the severity of and shorten recovery from exacerbations (oral route, when possible; 30 to 50mg daily for 5 days) | I | Strong

claims.claim: Antibiotics amoxycillin or doxycycline for 5 days where clinical features of infection (increased volume and colour change of sputum and/or fever) — I, Strong
claims.source_text: Consider prescribing antibiotic therapy (amoxycillin or doxycycline for 5 days) for COPD exacerbations with clinical features of infection (increased volume and change in colour of sputum and/or fever) | I | Strong

claims.claim: Oxygen target SpO2 88% to 92% to improve survival — II, Strong; controlled delivery 0.5 to 2.0 L/min — II, Strong
claims.source_text: Use supplemental oxygen for hypoxaemia in COPD exacerbations, target SpO₂ 88% to 92% to improve survival | II | Strong | Controlled oxygen delivery (0.5 to 2.0 L/min) is indicated for hypoxaemia in patients with exacerbations. | II | Strong

claims.claim: NIV improves survival in acute hypercapnic respiratory failure — I, Strong
claims.source_text: | Non-invasive ventilation improves survival for people with COPD and acute hypercapnic respiratory failure | I | Strong |

claims.claim: DECAF: derived from 920 patients, validated in 2,645 across 6 UK hospitals; components extended MRC Dyspnoea, eosinopenia, consolidation, acidaemia, atrial fibrillation; AUROC 0.86 (0.82-0.89); score of 3 confers 27.2% 30-day mortality
claims.source_text: DECAF was derived with data from 920 consecutive patients ... The five strongest predictors of mortality that comprise the score are extended MRC Dyspnoea Score, eosinopenia, consolidation, acidaemia, and atrial fibrillation. The score showed high discrimination for mortality with an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve = 0.86, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.89. A DECAF score of 3 predicts confers a 27.2% 30-day mortality risk. Echevarria et al examined the performance of the DECAF score in 2,645 patients ... across 6 hospitals in the UK

claims.claim: PE in 16% of 880 hospitalised patients undergoing CTPA, range 3-29%; consider PE when infection signs absent and chest pain or cardiac failure present
claims.source_text: A systematic review comprising seven studies with a total of 880 patients who were hospitalised with an exacerbation of COPD and underwent a CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) found that 16% had a PE ... (3% to 29%) ... A diagnosis of PE should be considered in patients presenting with an exacerbation of COPD when signs of respiratory infection are absent, and chest pain or cardiac failure are present

claims.claim: STATCOPE: simvastatin 40mg daily for at least 12 months did not affect exacerbation rates or time to first exacerbation (evidence level II)
claims.source_text: Simvastatin at a daily dose of 40 mg for at least 12 months did not affect exacerbation rates or the time to a first exacerbation (Criner 2014) [evidence level II]

claims.claim: Evidence surveillance paused; updates less frequent during transition; announcement 15 Jul 2026
claims.source_text: we've temporarily paused our regular evidence surveillance cycle ... COPD-X evidence reviews and updates will occur less frequently during this transition. Published on: 15-07-2026
